$comment: Updates this repo has decided not to take yet. Read by scripts/check-dependency-updates.ts,
which fails on any compatible update — patch, minor, or prerelease-to-stable — that a pin has
not taken. An entry here downgrades that failure to a warning until its date; it never hides it.
`until` is exclusive: a deferral dated 2026-09-01 stops applying on 2026-09-01. Give a reason a
reader in three months can act on — what breaks, and what has to happen first.
`manifest` scopes an entry to one manifest; omit it and the entry speaks for every pin of that
name, which is wrong whenever the same package is pinned twice for different reasons.
`acceptedVulnerabilities` is the other half: a vulnerability this repo ships with, because the
install delay in bunfig.toml is never punctured — not even to reach a fix. A release published
days ago is how a compromised package arrives, so the delay outranks a known CVE, and when the
only fix is too young the vulnerability is carried instead. Each entry pairs one advisory with
one lockfile, matching an `sca.exclusions` entry in .fluidattacks/sca.yaml, which is where the
scanner is told to stop counting it. The reason and the expiry live here because that config
has nowhere to put them. An exclusion with no entry fails, an expired entry fails, and so does
an entry whose exclusion is gone.

acceptedVulnerabilities.reason: brace-expansion 5.0.7 reaches this install through @stryker-mutator/core's minimatch. Every release <= 5.0.7 is affected (High, denial of service via unbounded expansion) and the fix, 5.0.8, was published 2026-07-23 — inside the 7-day install delay, which holds. What runs here is a build-time mutation runner expanding this repo's own glob patterns, so nothing untrusted reaches the parser. 5.0.8 becomes installable on 2026-07-30: pin it via `overrides` then, and delete this entry together with the exclusion in .fluidattacks/sca.yaml.
